question.text: Social Enterprises in India can access which of the following funding channels?

answer.text: Only donations and grants (no venture capital permitted)
Only social venture capital funds (SVFs) as Category I AIFs
Both donations/grants and social venture capital funds, including impact investors and incubators
Only CSR-linked funding from Schedule VII-compliant donors

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Ch 1.3, both For-Profit and Non-Profit Social Enterprises can access grants, donations, social venture capital funds, and multilateral agency funding. Organizations like Acumen Fund, Villgro and Intellecap invest in SEs alongside CSR and grant capital. The Trap: Option A artificially limits funding to philanthropy — incorrect. Option B limits to SVFs only. Option D limits to CSR only. The chapter explicitly notes SEs use a plurality of funding channels. Cross-Exam Context: Cross-links to XIX-A/B/C/D/E (AIF) where SVFs are Category I AIFs, and to V-A (MF Distributor) where donor-side 80G deductions apply. SIAs must understand the funding stack to test funds-flow evidence. Assessor's Pro-Tip: During SAS-1100 engagements, reconcile inflows by source: grant letters (donor-side), SVF term sheets (investor-side), CSR contribution receipts (Schedule VII), and ZCZP proceeds (SSE). Different sources trigger different disclosure obligations in the AIR.
